Caveat: this scaffold.py was authored by the model itself during the run — no skill tooling was staged in the bare config — but the rubric as written is satisfied on substance, not surface.

weak.assertion: scaffold.py plan and verify were both run
weak.reason: In the bare config no scaffold.py was staged, yet this passed because the model wrote its own cwd/scripts/scaffold.py and ran plan/verify on it. The assertion names a generic filename, not the skill's staged script path or plan schema, so it cannot distinguish the skill's tooling from ad-hoc self-built tooling. If the intent is to measure the skill's lifecycle specifically, pin the script provenance (staged path) or a schema fingerprint of its plan output.

weak.assertion: the audit settled by gate.py verdict with zero gaps
weak.reason: gate.py verdict settles whatever findings file it is handed; the model authored out/Billing/.audit-findings.json itself with an empty findings list, so a model that self-declares zero findings gets 'pass' regardless of tree conformance. Expectation 1's on-disk host-project check partially compensates, but the verdict clause alone would pass a nonconformant tree with a hollow findings file.

uncovered: gate.py coverage reported both mechanical rules uncovered (manifest_absent: true, uncovered: central-package-management, module-skeleton-structure); no assertion requires the mechanical layer to be audited by hand when the analyzer manifest is missing — here the self-built verify happened to cover them, but nothing in the rubric demands it.

The headline finding for a baseline comparison: a strong bare model scored 4/4 on this rubric by inventing equivalent tooling on the fly, so this rubric as written measures the outcome (boundary held, skeleton conformant) rather than the skill's contribution; the skill-vs-bare delta on this case will be time/cost/reliability, not rubric pass rate.
rubric_feedback.overall: All four assertions passed on genuine evidence, but two hinge on artifacts the model can self-author (its own scaffold.py, its own empty findings file), so the rubric does not separate skill-staged tooling from a capable bare model on this case.
